nodes.title: Expected number of hires as a real harmonic sum

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a list of $n$ pairwise distinct elements of a linearly ordered type, and rearrange its entries by a uniformly random permutation of the indices. The expected number of hires, valued in $[0, \infty]$, that the hire-assistant procedure (interview the entries in order, hiring each one strictly better than every earlier one) makes on the rearranged list equals $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Expected number of hires under a random permutation

nodes.summary: For every nonempty list of $n$ candidates in a linearly ordered type, the number of hires $h$ recorded in the cost pair of the hire-assistant scan satisfies $1 \le h \le n$.
nodes.title: Hire-count bounds for the hire-assistant scan

nodes.summary: For every list $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ in a linearly ordered type, the list of indices hired by the hire-assistant scan, in chronological order, is the increasing list of all indices $i < n$ such that $x_j < x_i$ for every $j < i$.
nodes.title: The hire-assistant scan hires exactly the strict prefix maxima

nodes.summary: For every strictly increasing list $x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_{n-1}$ in a linearly ordered type, including the empty list, the hire-assistant scan hires the indices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ in that order, and its cost pair is $(n, n)$.
nodes.title: Strictly increasing input hires every candidate

nodes.summary: On the empty list, the hire-assistant scan returns no manager and an empty list of hires, with cost pair $(0, 0)$.
nodes.title: Hire-assistant scan on no candidates

nodes.summary: For every list $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ in a linearly ordered type, the manager returned by the hire-assistant scan is none when the list is empty, and otherwise is the smallest index $i$ such that $x_i$ is a maximum of the list.
nodes.title: The hire-assistant scan returns the earliest best candidate

nodes.summary: For every element $a$ of a linearly ordered type, on the one-element list $[a]$ the hire-assistant scan returns manager index $0$ and hire list $[0]$, with cost pair $(1, 1)$: the single candidate is hired regardless of its quality.
nodes.title: Hire-assistant scan on one candidate

nodes.summary: For every list of $n$ candidates in a linearly ordered type, the cost pair of the hire-assistant scan is $(n, h)$, where $h$ is the length of the list of hired indices that the scan returns.
nodes.title: Cost of the hire-assistant scan

nodes.summary: Given candidates $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ in a linearly ordered type, the scan interviews them in order while keeping a current manager, initially none, which counts as below every candidate. Candidate $i$ is hired exactly when $x_i$ is strictly greater than the value of the current manager, and then becomes the new manager; ties keep the earlier manager. nodes.title: The hire-assistant scan

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
